items.title: Crusoe confirms its developer role and details the campus energy design
items.note: Crusoe says it is developing Google’s Armstrong County campus, which broke ground in June 2025, and directly connects to Serena’s Goodnight 1 and Goodnight 2 wind farms, each rated at 265.5 megawatts. The company says Goodnight 1 is operating, Goodnight 2 is under construction, surplus wind generation can flow to the grid, and the campus will use closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling. Its statement reports more than 5,500 skilled laborers onsite daily; the basis is not reconciled with the more than 7,500 current workers reported at the September 23 open house. These are company statements—not independent operating measurements.

items.title: Project Llano sponsors disclose construction and resource estimates
items.note: At the open house, Crusoe said the six-building campus should turn over its first buildings to Google in early 2027 and finish construction by year-end. It reported more than 7,500 current workers, 50 planned permanent jobs, construction water use averaging about 600,000 gallons per day during early work and declining toward 275,000 as buildings are enclosed, and about 2 million gallons per operating building each year through closed-loop cooling. Sponsors also described the Goodnight wind farms as the primary power source, ERCOT as backup, and more than $850 million in projected lifetime local tax revenue. These are company estimates—not permits, measured operating results, or government findings.

items.title: Armstrong County open house draws community concerns
items.note: KVII confirms the Google–Crusoe open house occurred at Claude High School. A resident described concern about protecting her ranch and legacy; Crusoe said it plans a long-term partnership with Google and aims to be a responsible neighbor. Those are attributed statements, not government findings or changes to the project’s specifications.

items.title: Homeowner files two challenges to Microsoft expansion annexation
items.note: Cowboy State Daily reports that Heather Madrid Donis filed two petitions in Laramie County District Court challenging Cheyenne’s roughly 3,460-acre July annexation for Microsoft’s proposed expansion. The petitions allege an incorrect landowner designation and an Open Meetings Act violation tied to an August 10 council action; the city declined to comment on pending litigation. These are unresolved allegations in filed petitions—not court findings, an invalidation of the annexation, or evidence that construction has stopped.

items.title: Custer County supervisors hear proposed data-center regulations; final action remains pending
items.note: The Board of Supervisors held a public hearing on regulations unanimously recommended by the Planning Commission on September 23. The draft addresses water and cooling, noise, electrical demand, emergency response, setbacks, decommissioning, and community-benefit agreements. No one spoke during the supervisors’ hearing, and the board did not adopt the rules; a resolution is expected at a future meeting.

items.title: Arevia-linked LLC options more than 560 acres northwest of Lincoln
items.note: Recorded four-year options identify Coffee Grounds Data LLC and Arevia Power development officer Ricardo Graf. Graf says the property is only undergoing early-stage site diligence and no development plan exists; the options create a right—not an obligation—to buy, and no rezoning, permit, construction, water, or power commitment is verified.

items.title: Nebraska appoints a 17-member Data Center Task Force
items.note: The DWEE-led group will evaluate effects on water resources, power grids, local infrastructure, zoning tools, and policy safeguards.

items.title: Fermi names NAES to prepare and operate the natural-gas generation fleet
items.note: Fermi says it will retain ownership and control of the generation assets while NAES establishes operating and maintenance procedures, work-management systems, training, risk reviews, and reliability programs, then supplies operating crews as units come online. This is pre-operational planning—not evidence that the delivered turbines are installed, commissioned, or generating electricity—and Fermi announced no new first-power date.

items.title: Fermi signs CBRE to operate and maintain Building One
items.note: Fermi says the five-year agreement begins when Building One is ready for service; CBRE transition work starts only after Fermi issues a notice to proceed. The contract is pre-operational planning and does not establish that the building is complete or serving compute.

items.title: TensorWave lease closing is extended to October 31
items.note: Fermi and TensorWave moved the 222-megawatt lease closing from September 30 while guaranty, work letters, operating schedules, board approvals, and sufficient project financing remain closing conditions. Fermi says the other lease terms remain in effect; the extension is not a completed closing.

items.title: Governor’s Office records response provides little detail on July Oracle meeting
items.note: Searchlight New Mexico reports that the Governor’s Office completed a request for notes, agendas, emails, and correspondence about Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham’s July 27 meeting with Oracle by producing only a photo of an iMessage schedule. Oracle met with the governor the same day an air-permit hearing officer favored a later hearing; the hearing was advanced two days later. An environmental advocate alleged possible influence, while the governor’s spokesperson described the meeting as a general update and denied interference. The records response does not establish a connection or improper influence, and it changes no permit ruling.

items.title: Companies report flooding reached the campus without critical-infrastructure damage
items.note: Oracle and STACK say floodwater reached Project Jupiter during the Southern New Mexico emergency, that no critical infrastructure was damaged, and that they are working with partners and insurers on site impacts. Their statement says the project remains on its planned schedule; this is a company assessment, not an independent engineering or government damage finding.

items.title: Oracle invokes protection against a possible 2028 delivery delay
items.note: CNBC reports that Oracle sent the Blue Owl unit developing Project Jupiter a force-majeure notice that could allow delayed payments if the campus misses its 2028 online target. Oracle said the project remains on its planned schedule and that it remains committed to New Mexico; Blue Owl said the notice does not change the project’s financial commitments. The notice is contractual risk mitigation—not a confirmed delay, default, cancellation, or construction halt.
